# Cross-Language Wire Protocol Roundtrip Tests — Design Spec (extracted)

> Auto-extracted from docs/wire-protocol-roundtrip-tests.md at decide-time.

## Decisions

### Test vectors live in styrene-rs under tests/fixtures/wire/ — generated by styrened tooling, consumed by both sides (decided)

Vectors live where the primary consumer (Rust tests) can find them without cross-repo fetching. A Python generator script in styrened/tools/generate_wire_vectors.py produces the vectors; the checked-in output lives in styrene-rs. styrened's reverse-direction tests reference the fixtures path via a submodule or pinned git ref. Same placement logic as the wire IDL schema: generated artifacts live with the implementation that owns the canonical wire format definition (styrene-rs/styrene-mesh).

### Both binary blobs and JSON sidecars: binary for byte-exactness assertion, JSON for human-readable debugging and hand-authoring (decided)

Binary .bin files are the ground truth for roundtrip tests — Rust and Python decoders must produce byte-identical output. JSON .json sidecars (same basename) describe field values and serve as human-readable source for debugging drift and hand-authoring new test cases without running the Python generator. The Python generator produces both from the same message definition. Binary-only makes drift debugging opaque; JSON-only loses the byte-exactness guarantee that is the whole point of cross-language tests.

### styrene-rs CI owns the cross-language matrix job — generates fresh vectors via Python, tests both Rust decode and Python decode in one job (decided)

styrene-rs already owns cargo test for the wire protocol. The cross-language job extends this: (1) runs Python generator to produce fresh vectors, (2) Rust roundtrip tests decode and re-encode to byte-identical output, (3) Python decoder tests run against Rust-generated vectors. Single job, single ownership, one place to investigate failures. styrened CI verifies its own encode/decode consistency independently but does not own the cross-language matrix. Requires only a Python dev dependency in styrene-rs CI (already present for styrene-native PyO3 build tooling).
